newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France cargo ex-chief denies quarrel.
newsitem.headline: Air France cargo ex-chief denies quarrel.

text.p: Former Air France cargo director Sten Grotenfelt said there had been "differences in style" in the airline's management over a project to transform the cargo division into a subsidiary firm.
But he denied there had been any quarrel with the chairman and said his decision to quit earlier this month resulted from "a number of short-term issues" which he didn't want to elaborate on.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, he highlighted union resistance to the project to transform Air France's cargo division into a subsidiary company, which provoked strike action in the division last October.

"Air France's chairman and executives agree that the future of the division lies with this kind of structure, but let's say there was a difference in management styles on how to bring it about," he added.

Grotenfelt said: "I've quit without any acrimony or bitterness. Contrary to reports in the press, there was no quarrel with Air France chairman, Christian Blanc for whom I have a good deal of respect."
He added: "Air France Cargo has a great future and is doing reasonably well at a time when it is difficult to make money out of air cargo."
Grotenfelt said he had no immediate plans but confirmed he would be staying in the air cargo industry.

A company source told Reuters earlier this week: "Grotenfelt was appointed to revamp Air France's cargo activites and under his leadership the division has made a satisfactory recovery following the low point of end-1993 when a three-week strike took place. His mission can be seen as completed."
Grotenfelt joined Air France in June 1994 from Cargolux where he had been the cargo airline's president and chief executive.
Francois Bachelet, Air France Cargo's Strategy director and formerly Europe director is replacing Grotenfelt as head of the cargo division, the airline said.
Major up and coming projects in Air France's cargo division include the creation of a new express unit and a state-of-the-art warehousing complex at CDG, named G1XL.
The Air France group is currently finalising merger plans with its subsidiary, Air France Europe, due to take effect, April 1 1997. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 542 7706 Fax+5017
